evidence: The pull-request selection compares each member's path to git's canonical names by string equality (src/gates/red-witness.ts storedWitnessEvaluated: `facts.mutated.some((file) => facts.changed.has(file))`, with `mutated` built from `member.file` verbatim at :464-:474), while the harness that applies the mutation accepts any spelling `join` normalises (src/witness/run.ts:876 `join(cloneDir, member.file)`) and the spec schema constrains `file` only to `\S` (src/gates/schemas/witness-spec.schema.json, `file`). So `./scripts/x.mjs` mutates the right file and is never matched by a diff that lists `scripts/x.mjs`.

MEASURED at 55a7850 through the real CLI (`node bin/tiphys.ts gates run --registry gate-registry.yaml --mode full --event pull_request --only red-witness`, node v26.6.0, scratch clone of the head with the witness directory cut to three specs): base B2 holds `witness/m5-p3-missing-review-is-red.json` with member 0 `file` respelled `./scripts/check-dual-review.mjs` as a STORED spec; the pull request appends a line to `scripts/check-dual-review.mjs` and to `src/plan.ts`. Result: `green: 3 witness(es): 0 own, 1 stored evaluated ..., 2 stored skipped (no file they mutate or run changed)`, exit 0, although the diff changed the file that member mutates. Same head, `--event push`: `3 stored evaluated, 0 stored skipped`, exit 0 (nothing was actually broken, so this shows the skip, not a false pass).

WHY IT IS LOW. Introducing the spelling through the gate is refused: the same respelling committed together with the source change as an OWN spec is `red: rule (d): declared dangerous state does not intersect the phase diff (member 0, mutation of ./scripts/check-dual-review.mjs)`, exit 1. Audited paths (src/, bin/, plugin/src/) are additionally held by the coverage rule, which uses the same spelling and so reddens a changed source file whose only spec is respelled. The entry the gate does not see is a witness-only pull request: the same respelling as the only change gives `not-applicable: precondition red-witness-diff evaluated and unmet: no changed path under src/, bin/, plugin/`. No instance exists today: a derivation over all 419 specs at the head (loadWitnessSpec then memberTouchedFiles, each path tested against `git ls-files -z`) found 0 paths that are not tracked files, and 67 of the 419 guard at least one file outside src/, bin/ and plugin/src/ (27 members on .github/workflows/release.yml, 18 on scripts/release-verify.sh, 9 on schemas/verdict.schema.json), which is where coverage does not help.

Before M6-P8 the spelling could not matter for correctness, because every stored witness was evaluated on every pull request that touched src/. The canonical spelling became load-bearing with this change.
findings.concrete-fix: In selectionFacts (src/gates/red-witness.ts), compare on `path.posix.normalize(file)` with a leading `./` removed, and treat any member whose path is absolute, contains `..`, or differs from its normalised form as triggered (evaluate it), so an odd spelling fails toward evaluation; optionally also refuse a non-canonical `file` or `patch` in parseWitnessSpec so a witness-only pull request cannot introduce one. Red-witness it with the respelled stored spec above (skipped today, evaluated after).

evidence: The selection watches two things: a file a member mutates (plus a patch member's own patch file) and a `*.test.ts` file under `test/` that carries a named test (src/gates/red-witness.ts storedWitnessEvaluated and changedTestSources). This is exactly the plan's rule (M6-P8 step 3), so it is not a defect against the contract, but two inputs a stored witness depends on are not watched, and each makes the pull-request arm and the push arm disagree on one head.

(a) The behavior row. A witness's `behavior` must resolve in test/behaviors.json (rule (b), evaluated only for witnesses the run evaluates). MEASURED through the real CLI, scratch clone as above: the pull request deletes the `m5-p3-missing-review-is-red` row from test/behaviors.json and touches src/plan.ts. `--event pull_request`: `green: ... 1 stored evaluated ..., 2 stored skipped`, exit 0. `--event push`, same base and head: `red: ... 3 stored evaluated ... witness m5-p3-missing-review-is-red no longer guards its behavior (rule (b): behavior m5-p3-missing-review-is-red does not resolve in test/behaviors.json)`, exit 1. So a behavior-id rename or row removal passes the pull request and reddens `main`.

(b) Test support modules. A named test's file can import a helper that is not itself a `*.test.ts` file. A derivation over the 419 stored specs (named tests resolved by the harness's own `includes` rule, then relative imports read from each test file) found 43 whose test file imports `test/support/dual-review-registry.ts` (37) or `test/support/remove-git-directory.ts` (6). MEASURED: the pull request appends a line to test/support/dual-review-registry.ts and to src/plan.ts: `--event pull_request` `1 stored evaluated, 2 stored skipped` (the witness whose tests use that helper is skipped), `--event push` evaluates all three.

What bounds it: the push run on `main` does evaluate every stored witness, and it runs on the same diff whenever the pull-request arm ran (same `diff-touches` precondition on src/, bin/, plugin/), so the divergence surfaces as a RED push run, not silently. A helper change that breaks a test is still caught before merge by the `suite` gate; only a helper change that keeps the test green while it stops reaching the mutated arm is invisible until the sweep. DR-0066 accepts checks moving to the push run, so this is recorded rather than blocking.
findings.concrete-fix: Cheapest: trigger a stored witness on a pull request when test/behaviors.json differs between the merge base and the head in the row for its `behavior` (two `git show` reads, one JSON compare), and when any changed file under test/ that is not a `*.test.ts` is imported by a test file carrying one of its named tests (the import scan in the derivation above is ten lines). If the owner prefers the plan's narrower rule to stand, state both unwatched inputs in the work history and in STATE.md as the known cost of DR-0066, so a red push run from either is read as this and not as a flake.

evidence: Not a code defect: the owner's concern for hazard 2 (the full sweep never runs) has a scheduling form the change does not touch. The workflow's concurrency block is `group: gates-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (.github/workflows/gates.yml:9-11); on a push the ref is refs/heads/main for every merge, so merge N+1 cancels the still-running run for head N (CLAUDE.md T-009, measured on 5ec129e).

Duration of the thing now running on push: the work history's own run 1 at bbe5133 measured `34 stored evaluated in 441310ms` (12.98 s each) and run 3 `34 stored evaluated in 428316ms`; at the head there are 419 specs, so about 416 stored on the push arm, roughly 416 x 8.7 s = 60 min (PR #229's rate, DR-0066) to 416 x 13 s = 90 min (this branch's rate), before the M1 exit test step, which is now push-only and is the LAST step of the job (.github/workflows/gates.yml, `M1 exit test (local mode)` after both gates steps), so a cancel or a red gates step also means it never runs. The work history records the same estimate under `Not done` and says it is not measured.

Consequence: a merge landing inside that window leaves the previous head's sweep and M1 exit test unfinished. That is a cancelled run, which is not green and is not read as green (T-009 says verify the current head's run), so no false pass; but the skipped witnesses of finding CR-M6P8A-02 and the M1 exit test are then only checked when some later push run is allowed to finish.
findings.concrete-fix: One line in the workflow: `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`, so a pull-request run is still superseded by a newer push to its branch but a `main` push run is queued rather than cancelled (GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the queue does not grow without bound). Or, without touching the workflow, record in STATE.md that the next merge waits for the post-merge run when the merge touched src/, bin/ or plugin/ (T-009's second option). Either way, quote the first completed push run's red-witness detail line as the p8-time evidence.

hazard-classes-addressed.probed: Read src/gates/red-witness.ts storedWitnessEvaluated and selectionFacts, computePhaseDiff (src/witness/run.ts:311, `diff -z --name-status --no-renames base...head`), resolveNamedTests (:750, `source.includes(name)`, the same rule the selection uses) and applyMember (:876). Ran the new tests once on node v26.6.0, dist built: test/gate-event-parameter.test.ts 1 tests 1 pass 0 fail 0 skipped; test/gate-registry.test.ts 20 tests 20 pass 0 fail 0 skipped; test/witness.test.ts 67 tests 67 pass 0 fail 0 skipped. Dangerous inputs tried through the REAL CLI on a scratch clone of the head (real gate-registry.yaml, three real witnesses): (1) a test file MOVED (`git mv test/dual-review.test.ts test/dual-review-moved.test.ts`, git reports `A test/dual-review-moved.test.ts`, `D test/dual-review.test.ts`) with the named test's witness stored: `2 stored evaluated, 1 stored skipped`, the witness whose test moved IS evaluated, exit 0; (2) a mutated file reached by a path spelled `./scripts/check-dual-review.mjs` on a stored spec: SKIPPED while the file changed, exit 0, recorded as CR-M6P8A-01 (an own spec with that spelling is refused by rule (d), a witness-only pull request is not-applicable); (3) a behavior row deleted and a test-support helper edited: skipped on the pull-request arm, evaluated on push, recorded as CR-M6P8A-02. A derivation over all 419 stored specs at the head: 0 member paths that are not tracked files, 0 specs with no mutated file, 0 patch members whose headers parse to no file. Rename-inside-a-file is held by the merge-base source read, a deleted test file and a deleted mutated file are both in the diff and evaluated (not skipped).

gate-registry.yaml red-witness is `events: [pull_request, push]`, `parameters: [base, head, event]` (diff against ae6ac9b: events was `[pull_request]`). The gate reads the event only from `--event` (src/gates/red-witness.ts parseArgs and `run.event`); `storedWitnessEvaluated` returns true for anything but the literal `pull_request`, so push and no event both take the full sweep, and an event other than the two is `error`. The runner passes `--event` only when the run named one (src/gates/run.ts:1589-1595) and the workflow's push step names it literally (`--event push`, .github/workflows/gates.yml). Measured through the real CLI on a scratch clone, same base and head, three runs: `--event pull_request`: `1 stored evaluated ..., 1 stored skipped (no file they mutate or run changed)`; `--event push`: `2 stored evaluated ..., 0 stored skipped (event push evaluates every stored witness)`; no `--event`: `2 stored evaluated ..., 0 stored skipped (event none evaluates every stored witness)`; all exit 0. The plan's acceptance for this arm is red-witnessed by witness/m6-p8-push-evaluates-every-stored.json (dangerous state `facts.event !== "pull_request"` becoming `facts.event === undefined`). The scheduling form of this hazard, a push sweep that a later merge cancels, is CR-M6P8A-03.

computePhaseDiff returns ok:false when either revision does not resolve, when merge-base/diff exits nonzero, or when git cannot run (src/witness/run.ts:203 gitIn: ok only on exit 0, a spawn error or a 256 MiB maxBuffer overrun is a failure), and runRedWitnessGate returns `error` before any selection (src/gates/red-witness.ts, `the phase diff could not be computed, so no stored witness is skipped`); the merge-base source read of a changed test file also errors rather than skipping. Measured: `node src/gates/red-witness.ts --base 0000000000000000000000000000000000000001 --head <sha> --event pull_request` prints `red-witness: error (the phase diff could not be computed, so no stored witness is skipped: the base revision ... does not resolve ...`; an unresolvable `--head` prints the same with `the head revision`; through the runner `gates run ... --event pull_request --base 000...1` reports `red-witness: error: git diff -z --no-renames --name-only ... exited 128: fatal: Invalid symmetric difference expression`, `1 gate(s) reported error`, exit 21 (the diff-touches precondition fails first, also to error). An empty diff is not an uncomputable one and cannot reach this gate with the precondition met, because the precondition reads the same `base...head` with the same flags. Workflow: `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still runs `npm ci`, `npm run build`, then `Gates (pull request)` or `Gates (push)`, and the `M1 exit test (local mode)` step carries `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so it runs on push; no step runs `npm test` on its own.
hazard-classes-addressed.cleared-because: An unresolvable base or head is `error`, never a selection over an empty change set, through both the gate CLI and the registry runner (measured above), and the full-history and shallow-clone refusals that precede the diff are unchanged.
